improvements.title: Run and publish the first on-silicon FI campaign on the U585: RDP-2 fetch, FSBL verify chain, gated_unlock, c10 ct_eq gate
improvements.threat: Every FI gate in the tree is evidenced only by source shape, host tests and Unicorn emulation; HW-ASSUME-RDP2 (RDP-2 resists glitching) is the single highest-leverage unverified premise. Bozzato/Focardi 2019 downgraded RDP-2→RDP-1 on STM32F373 with one 11 µs glitch; Kraken/Unciphered did the same class on F2/F4; Donjon glitched Safe 3's MCU integrity check; μ-Glitch defeated TZ-M on the L5 sibling; Šimoník reports ~76% PIN-check bypass on a U5 sibling. Neither Trezor nor Ledger has published a U5 data point.
improvements.proposal: Treat it as a release gate with receipts: (1) Scaffold/ChipWhisperer-Husky crowbar + PicoEMP campaign on a sacrificial RDP-2 pq1 board, sweeping the boot-time option-byte fetch (RDP/TZEN latch) for RDP-1 behaviour; (2) glitch sweep of fsbl::filter_valid + verify_images with a deliberately corrupted slot (goal: branch into unsigned slot); (3) gated_unlock pre-commit bump and the SE verdict sentinel with a wrong PIN (goal: unlock or no page-124 charge); (4) c10_sign_verified ct_eq/verify gate with a grafting oracle (Genêt's SPHINCSplus-FA tooling) to measure exploitable-fault rate with the double-compute ON vs OFF; (5) fixed-vs-random TVLA (1k traces) on the secret-seed PRF to put a number on F-16. Publish scripts + traces under tools/bench as reproducible evidence (Ledger does not publish its own).
improvements.rationale: Converts 'countermeasures present' into 'countermeasures measured' and either closes HW-ASSUME-RDP2 or forces the design to stop leaning on it. Both the FSBL (frozen forever after RDP-2 per invariant #10) and the first-boot ceremony depend on this answer, so it must precede the shipping ceremony, not follow it.

improvements.title: Hardware-in-the-loop voltage-glitch sensing: arm PVD (~2.8 V) → zeroize, pin BOR_LEV high in the ship profile and the tripwire, and configure ADC4 analog watchdogs on VDD/VBUS/VREFINT so ITAMP7/12/13 wipe via TAMP confirmed mode
improvements.threat: USB-C VBUS is the only supply and the primary glitch-injection point; today nothing in firmware bounds the dwell window on the rails. The BOR is at the 1.71 V default, PVD is disabled, and the ADC4-backed internal tampers (ITAMP7/12/13) are armed in tamp.rs but have no ADC behind them, so they can never fire. μ-Glitch had to defeat the L5 brown-out detector to succeed — a raised BOR plus PVD is the cheapest bar-raiser on this silicon.
improvements.proposal: (a) Pin BOR_LEV = level 4 (~2.8 V for a 3V3 part) in SHIP_PROFILE_U585, make lockdown::bor_lev_ok load-bearing (currently 'still being pinned'), and include it in both the FSBL tz-1 tripwire and first-boot Phase A. (b) Secure-world PVD driver: PWR_SVMCR PVDLS=level 5, PVDE=1, EXTI line secure, PVD_PVM_IRQn at highest secure priority → zeroize_sensitive_state + relock (not a halt). (c) Configure ADC4 in continuous mode on VREFINT/VDD (and the VBUS sense if routed) with tight AWD1/2/3 windows, so ITAMP7/12/13 trip in hardware under CR3=0 confirmed mode → BKP erase + intrusion wipe with no software in the loop. (d) Enable the ECC double-error / CSS NMI path tracked as #21-tamp-css_pvd. Run ITAMP rail-glitch characterisation as part of FI-01.
improvements.rationale: Trezor ships PVD at 2.8 V + BOR level 4 + the same ITAMP set, but even Trezor leaves the ADC watchdogs un-driven ('never triggered'); driving ADC4 turns an existing hardware-enforced tamper into a real voltage-glitch detector, which no wallet vendor currently does on U5. PVD/BOR are slow (µs) and will not catch ns crowbars, but they catch cheap USB-supply attacks and constrain glitch parameters for the rest.

improvements.title: FSBL verify-chain FI bundle before the range freezes: TRNG-driven delays, default-poisoned jump target set only after the full chain, volatile secbool staircase across slot admission, tail-padding check, and checksum-redundant C10 verify
improvements.threat: The FSBL becomes physically immutable after RDP-2 (invariant #10), so any FI weakness in it is permanent. Today: wait_random uses the constant 0x42 (an attacker's second fault needs no new timing, so check_true's double-eval collapses to one setup); the branch target is a plain `Slot` enum flowing through `Option` (niche-encoded, one bit from `None` to `Some(Slot::A)`) with no final re-check before into_slot; verify_images hashes only secure_len/ns_len bytes and never checks the slot tail, so attacker-written gadgets after the signed image survive; the C10 verifier is one code path, and Wagner et al. 2023 / BSI-AISEC 2025 show a faulted WOTS checksum during VERIFICATION accepts forged signatures.
improvements.proposal: (1) Bring up the RNG peripheral in the FSBL (RCC clock + TRNG, same driver as hw/rng.rs) so fsbl::fi::wait_random draws TRNG lengths; fail = halt. (2) Trezor next_stage_addr pattern: a `volatile u32 next_stage = 0` written with the slot's secure address only as the last statement after filter_valid + verify_images + tz-1 + render all return OK_SENTINEL; into_slot takes that address, so a skipped check branches to 0 (reset vector/fault), never into a slot. (3) Replace the Option/enum flow with volatile Hamming-distant verdict words per stage (manifest_ok, images_ok, optbytes_ok, render_ok) folded with an AND over sentinels, and a triple redundant compare immediately before the branch (Trezor firmware_present/backup). (4) verify_images: after hashing, scan secure_len..SLOT_SECURE_CAPACITY and ns_len..SLOT_NS_CAPACITY and require a uniform 0xFF/0x00 fill (Trezor check_image_contents). (5) Make the signature verify redundant with independent inputs: verify once, wait_random, verify again with the WOTS target-sum/checksum recomputed from a separately-copied message digest, and compare the two root outputs under ct_eq before the sentinel; add a Hamming-distant `sigmask/sigmask_inv`-style step mask that must equal the expected set at exit. (6) Set MSPLIM in the FSBL (fsbl/src/main.rs:172 note). Land a rainbow sweep for fsbl::verify_images (#591) as the regression test.
improvements.rationale: This is the EF-swarm F15 'FI-hardened FSBL image verify' gate plus the Trezor boardloader patterns, bundled because they all touch the frozen range and must land before the WRP/RDP-2 ceremony. Each closes a distinct single-fault class (retiming, jump-target, data-flow, hidden tail, verifier checksum) that the current sentinel-only gating does not.

improvements.title: Always-on secure Random Delay Interrupt (floating-mean, refreshed at every NSC veneer / USB packet) plus a non-reusing TRNG policy for all countermeasure delays on master
improvements.threat: Jitter exists only at annotated wait_random call sites; every linear path between them (USB-triggered dispatch before the first wait_random, the multi-second C10 sign, SE tunnel setup, LCD render windows) is trigger-lockable from an externally observable event. Separately, master's FI-delay fallback reuses the last good TRNG byte on SECS/CECS, so a glitcher that latches the TRNG into error collapses every delay to a constant (the no-reuse rework exists only on perf/flash-opt-level-z).
improvements.proposal: (1) Secure-only periodic timer (TIM2/TIM3 are already SAU-secured; or a secure SysTick slot) firing every 1 ms with a cycle-exact asm wait of `drbg8() + session_delay` where session_delay is a second TRNG-seeded byte refreshed only on externally observable events: NSC veneer entry (nsc/mod.rs dispatcher), USB packet receipt, button edge. Keep an FihBool `rdi_enabled` and treat a corrupted value as a fault. Pause only inside the ~µs-critical SPI/I2C timing windows that cannot tolerate it, and prove those windows are not FI-critical. (2) Feed it from a ChaCha/AES-CTR DRBG seeded from the TRNG (reseed every N draws) so the 1 kHz draw does not starve rng_strong. (3) Merge #834/#835 option-2 onto master: a failed TRNG draw fails the operation (not halt, not reuse), and RDI switches to 'fault' on TRNG error. (4) Budget check: ~255 cycles/ms ≈ 0.2 % at 160 MHz; re-measure test-key-speed.
improvements.rationale: Trezor has shipped RDI since 2019 (Clavier/Coron/Dabbous floating mean); Donjon's DS28C36 double-fault paper concludes double verification 'is not efficient enough if it is used alone' and must be combined with hardware and/or software jitter. pq1's signer is stronger than Trezor's per-site, but site-based jitter leaves the attacker a profiled linear path to each gate.

improvements.title: Fault-detected ⇒ escalate: charge the three-way PIN budget on every sentinel/CFI/receipt trip, re-entrant fault ⇒ wipe, and zeroize SRAM before any glitch halt
improvements.threat: Every FI detection today ends in a refusal (return FAIL_SENTINEL / relock) or a bare `wfe` loop with master_secret still in SRAM and HandlerGuard suppressing the idle wipe. A stolen unlocked-capable device can therefore be glitch-characterised indefinitely: each failed attempt costs nothing, and a halt leaves the secrets resident for the next pulse.
improvements.proposal: (1) A single `fi::handle_fault(code)` sink (Trezor handle_fault + WF_ERROR_FATAL policy): static FihBool `in_progress` — a fault reported while one is being handled ⇒ immediate dual-SE admin wipe + page-125 flag; otherwise charge page 124 via pin_attempts_bump (which also advances E120/UserID on the next unlock by construction of the directional reconciliation), read back `pre+1`, zeroize_sensitive_state, then reset. Route check_true_into_sentinel failures at authorization sites, CfiCounter mismatches, ct_eq mismatches in c10_sign_verified, SCP03/CCM receipt failures, read_volatile_voted CounterUnstable, and `default:` arms of the fw_update/first-boot/sign-dispatch state machines through it. (2) halt_on_glitch and the panic path: zeroize SRAM secrets + TAMP BKERASE (BHK regs) + mask interrupts before `wfe`, on a fresh stack (Trezor call_with_new_stack); FSBL halt stays bare (no secrets). (3) Encode the state machines' phase words as sparse random u32s so a flipped enum lands in `default:`. Decide explicitly (owner) that genuine faults consume attempts — Trezor accepts this.
improvements.rationale: Bounds the attacker's glitch trials to the 10-attempt budget before self-destruction and makes the fault handler itself fault-hardened; cheap because every primitive (bump, admin wipe, zeroize, page-125 flag) already exists and only the policy wiring is missing. #835 H4 already adjudicated the halt-with-secrets problem; it is fixed only on a side branch.

improvements.title: Option-byte posture after RDP-2: persistent mismatch ⇒ wipe (not halt), silicon-pin the OEM1/OEM2 lock check and BOOT_LOCK, engage HDP1 over the FSBL at boot-exit, and assert BHKLOCK before the first SE/sign operation
improvements.threat: A regressed/altered option-byte set (RDP, TZEN, WRP, BOR, SECBOOTADD0, OEM keys) is the enabling state for every MCU-side attack. Today the FSBL tripwire halts with secrets intact (a halted device with intact secrets is a better glitch target than a wiped one); the OEM-lock gate fails closed only because it is unpinned, so an OEM2 password planted in transit is caught by a halt, not a verified detector; HDP1 is 0 so the FSBL pages remain readable all session; nothing asserts BHKLOCK is set before the SAES/BHK consumers run.
improvements.proposal: (1) Post-RDP-2 (TZEN+RDP=0xCC observed in the ship profile), route a persistent tz-1 mismatch in the secure world's own re-check (not the FSBL, which must stay write-free) to the intrusion wipe (BHK BKERASE + dual-SE admin wipe), keeping the FSBL halt as the pre-secret stage. (2) Close #46/#387: pin FLASH_NSSR OEM1LOCK/OEM2LOCK (register + bits) on a sacrificial RDP-0 board with a provisioned OEM1 key, flip OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED, and in Phase A write OEM1KEYR/OEM2KEYR = 0xFFFFFFFF before OPTSTRT as belt-and-braces; add BOOT_LOCK to the confirmed field set. (3) #39: HDP1EN + HDP1_PEND over pages 0..4 in the ship profile and HDP1_ACCDIS engaged by the secure world right after measured_boot (never by the FSBL). (4) bhk.rs: before the first SAES/BHK use and before every sign, read TAMP_SECCFGR and require BHKLOCK set through check_true_into_sentinel; unlocked ⇒ handle_fault. (5) Include BOR_LEV (FI-02) in the same confirmed set.
improvements.rationale: Trezor's shipped posture is 'option bytes exactly right or the device erases its BHK and repairs them' plus OEM-key clearing and HDP over the secret sector; pq1 cannot repair (invariant #10, read-only FSBL) but can wipe. RP2350's lesson: 'a software-write lock is not a fault-resistant lock' — detection must be followed by secret destruction, and every security-relevant latch (OEM, BOOT_LOCK, BHKLOCK) must be checked, not assumed.

improvements.title: SE-bound release of the entropy halves on a firmware measurement: each SE releases its half only after the measured-boot digest matches a value sealed at first boot, so a glitched FSBL/MCU integrity check cannot unlock funds
improvements.threat: Donjon's Safe 3 result is the concrete 'malicious hardware/firmware in the MCU' case: SE pairing secrets prove possession of a key, not what code is running, so a glitch on the MCU's own integrity check yields a reprogrammed device that still passes SE attestation. pq1 is structurally the same: OPTIGA PBS / SE050 SCP03 keys are DHUK/BHK-derived and any code running on the die can recompute them; a glitched FSBL verify (or an RDP downgrade) therefore still reaches both halves after PIN.
improvements.proposal: At first boot (Phase B), seal `M0 = SHA-256(fingerprint_digest_slotA ‖ fingerprint_digest_slotB_or_empty ‖ fsbl_digest ‖ option_byte_profile)` into each SE: OPTIGA as an AuthRef/confidentiality-protected data object whose read of half_O requires a session bound to a HMAC(M_current) proof via Shielded Connection (or as a key-derivation input into the PBS-equivalent session), SE050 by binding the UserID-protected object policy to a `HMAC-SHA256(K_se050_meas, M_current)` presented as part of the SCP03 session key derivation. The secure world recomputes M_current every boot from measured_boot::run (not the FSBL, since the FSBL is pre-secret) and derives the per-boot session material from it; a wrong measurement produces an undecryptable half rather than a visible refusal. Legitimate A/B updates re-seal under the PIN-gated fw_commit path (COMMIT already requires unlock) by writing the new M under the old session before the boot pointer flips, with a journaled rollback. Pair with a C10 MCU attestation (fingerprint-signed challenge) for the companion.
improvements.rationale: Moves the trust anchor for fund release from 'the MCU's integrity check was not glitched' to 'the SEs saw the expected measurement', which no public attack on an SE-less path can forge without also faulting the SE policy; it is the only design that makes a successful RDP downgrade or FSBL-verify glitch insufficient on its own. Trezor's May-2026 ML-DSA MCU attestation shows vendors are moving toward measured-MCU evidence, but none bind the seed release to it.

improvements.title: Timing canaries around FI-critical blocks (software Instruction Timer) and write→jitter→readback of the clock tree and TZ configuration
improvements.threat: CfiCounter catches skipped steps but not clock-glitch or stuck-at faults that leave the counter intact; the RCC/PLL setup is itself a fault target (μ-Glitch had to glitch the L5 PLL config to get under the BoD), and while sau.rs has a post-write readback the RCC path has none and neither inserts a random delay before the readback.
improvements.proposal: (1) `fi::TimedWindow`: snapshot a secure-only TIM (or DWT CYCCNT with LAR unlocked, secured) at block entry, compute the expected cycle envelope at build time per block (min/max with RDI jitter budget), and on exit require entry+min ≤ now ≤ entry+max through check_true_into_sentinel; apply to ct_eq of the two 4008-B sigs, verify-before-release, gated_unlock pre-commit → SE verdict, SCP03/CCM unwrap, SAU/GTZC/AIRCR setup and the first-boot RDP authorisation. Over/under-run ⇒ handle_fault (FI-05). (2) rcc.rs: after PLL/SWS switch, wait_random then re-read CFGR1/PLL1CFGR/PLL1DIVR and compare to the constants under a sentinel; mirror in the FSBL once it has a TRNG. (3) sau.rs: insert wait_random before each readback pass and add a second voted pass (read_volatile_voted) of SAU_RBAR/RLAR, GTZC SECCFGR and AIRCR, since the existing F6 verifier is a single pass.
improvements.rationale: NXP's LPC55 Code Watchdog pairs a secure counter with an instruction timer precisely because counters alone miss timing faults; RP2350's digital glitch detectors are the hardware form of the same idea. A software window on a secure timer is the closest U585 equivalent and is cheap. Readback after jitter is the standard answer to the μ-Glitch SAU/PLL targets.

improvements.title: Memory and counter integrity under faults: MSPLIM in both worlds, secrets in an ECC-NMI bank, an authentication tag over the page-123 live record set, and a non-trivial page-124 encoding
improvements.threat: A fault-induced stack-pointer corruption or deep recursion silently overwrites page-123/124 buffers (no MSPLIM anywhere); an SRAM bit-flip in master_secret/SLOT_CACHE corrupts silently (ECC double-error NMI off), which SLasH-DSA shows is exploitable during hash-based signing; a glitch or flash manipulation that drops the newest page-123 tally record lowers local_offchain_count with no detector; page 124 is a unary count of zero quadwords where an erased page decodes to 0 attempts (the exact 0xFF read-as-zero shape Trezor was defeated by via USB voltage manipulation).
improvements.proposal: (1) Program MSPLIM_S (and PSPLIM if used) 256 B above the stack base in the secure world's startup and in the FSBL; overflow ⇒ UsageFault ⇒ existing zeroize+reset path. (2) Place master_secret, SLOT_CACHE and the sign buffers in SRAM2 (or an ECC-enabled region per #48), enable RAMCFG ECC double-error NMI and route it to zeroize + handle_fault. (3) Page 123: maintain an HMAC-SHA256 (DHUK-rooted via saes_cmac) over the folded set of live per-slot counters written as the last quadword of each commit and verified on every read; mismatch ⇒ refuse to sign + handle_fault (Trezor STORAGE_TAG). (4) Page 124: replace the plain zero-quadword with a Hamming-structured marker (e.g. 01/10-expanded attempt index + complement) so neither 0x00…00 nor 0xFF…FF quadwords are well-formed, decode every copy and require agreement; keep the SE counters as primary. (5) Kani/rainbow fault-model tests for both decoders (the existing Kani work covers logic, not stuck-at reads).
improvements.rationale: These are shipped Trezor properties (MSPLIM, storage auth tag, blockwise 01/10 PIN counter) and a ship-blocker (#48); page-124 is the user-facing 10-attempt bound and page-123 is the off-chain cap, both read by FI-critical gates. Trezor explicitly justifies a simplified counter encoding when SE counters exist — pq1 is in the same position — but not an unencoded one.
